_about: Hand-labelled claims about OWASP NodeGoat (commit c5cb68a). 'real' = verified true by reading the source; 'false' = the source shows otherwise. Used by tests/eval_verifier.py to score the code verifier on a repo with known answers. Labels were checked against the source: e.g. the isAdmin guard on /benefits is commented out, so that claim is real; session.regenerate IS applied on signup but not on login. Note: NodeGoat's live code has password hashing commented out, so plaintext password storage is real.

findings.label: real
findings.title: Remote code execution through unsafe evaluation of contribution amounts
findings.description: The pension contributions form takes the pre-tax, after-tax and Roth percentages from the request and evaluates them as JavaScript instead of parsing numbers, so an attacker can run arbitrary code on the server.
steps_to_exploit: Submit the contributions form with a field containing JavaScript such as process.exit()

findings.label: real
findings.title: Any logged-in user can read other users' retirement allocations
findings.description: The allocations page takes the user id from the URL instead of the logged-in session, so changing the id in the path shows another user's allocation data.
findings.impact: Disclosure of other users' financial data.

findings.label: real
findings.title: Open redirect on the learning-resources link
findings.description: The learn endpoint redirects the browser to whatever address is in its url query parameter with no validation, so a trusted link can send victims to an attacker's site.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a link to the app's learn endpoint with url=https://evil.example
Send it to a logged-in user
They are redirected to the attacker's site

findings.label: real
findings.title: NoSQL injection in the allocations threshold filter
findings.description: The stock threshold from the query string is placed straight into a MongoDB $where JavaScript expression without validation, so an attacker can inject JavaScript into the database query.
findings.impact: Data disclosure and denial of service on the database.

findings.label: real
findings.title: Cross-site scripting because template auto-escaping is disabled
findings.description: The template engine is configured with auto-escaping turned off, so user-controlled values such as profile fields are written into pages unescaped.
steps_to_exploit: Save a profile first name containing a script tag
Load a page that renders it
The script runs in the victim's browser

findings.label: real
findings.title: Server-side request forgery in the research page
findings.description: The research page builds a URL from request parameters and fetches it from the server, returning the response body, so an attacker can make the server call internal addresses.
steps_to_exploit: Request the research page with url pointing at an internal service and a symbol value
The server fetches it and returns the content
findings.impact: Access to internal services and metadata endpoints.

findings.label: real
findings.title: No server-side CSRF protection on state-changing forms
findings.description: Forms such as the profile update can be submitted by any site the logged-in user visits because the server does not validate an anti-CSRF token.
steps_to_exploit: Host a page that auto-submits a POST to the profile update form
Get a logged-in user to open it

findings.label: real
findings.title: Session cookie lacks HttpOnly and Secure flags
findings.description: The session middleware is configured without cookie options, so the session cookie is readable by page scripts and sent over plain HTTP.

findings.label: real
findings.title: Session fixation at login
findings.description: After a successful login the existing session id is kept instead of being regenerated, so an attacker who planted a known session id can use it once the victim logs in.
steps_to_exploit: Make the victim use that id and log in
Reuse the same id as the logged-in victim

findings.label: real
findings.title: Login errors reveal whether a username exists
findings.description: The login page returns a different message for an unknown user name than for a wrong password, which lets an attacker enumerate valid accounts.
steps_to_exploit: Try many user names with a wrong password

findings.label: real
findings.title: Hard-coded session signing secret
findings.description: The secret used to sign session cookies is a fixed string committed in the configuration, so anyone with the source can forge or tamper with session cookies.
steps_to_exploit: Read the secret from the public repository
Sign a forged session cookie with it

findings.label: real
findings.title: User passwords are stored in plaintext in the database
findings.description: Passwords are saved exactly as the user typed them, so a database leak exposes every password.
steps_to_exploit: Gain read access to the users collection

findings.label: real
findings.title: Non-admin users can open the admin benefits page
findings.description: The benefits administration pages perform no role check, so any logged-in employee can view and edit every user's benefits.
steps_to_exploit: Log in as a normal user

findings.label: false
findings.title: SQL injection in the login query
findings.description: The login handler concatenates the user name into an SQL statement, so ' OR 1=1 -- logs in as anyone.
steps_to_exploit: Enter ' OR 1=1 -- as the user name

findings.label: false
findings.title: The dashboard is reachable without logging in
findings.description: The dashboard route has no authentication check, so an anonymous visitor can view it.
findings.impact: Exposure of account summaries to anonymous users.

findings.label: false
findings.title: Contribution updates can be submitted without being logged in
findings.description: The POST handler that updates pension contributions does not require a session, so an unauthenticated attacker can change contribution settings.
steps_to_exploit: Send a POST to /contributions with no cookie

findings.label: false
findings.title: Anonymous visitors can read any user's allocations
findings.description: The allocations route has no login requirement, so someone who is not signed in can request another user's allocation page directly.
findings.impact: Disclosure of financial data to the public.

findings.label: false
findings.title: Session id is not regenerated on signup
findings.description: When a new account is created the old session id is reused for the new logged-in session, allowing session fixation during registration.
steps_to_exploit: Plant a known session id in the victim's browser

findings.label: false
findings.title: Logout leaves the session valid on the server
findings.description: The logout handler only redirects the browser and never invalidates the server-side session, so a stolen session id keeps working after the user logs out.

findings.label: false
findings.title: The research page can be used without logging in
findings.description: The research route does not require a session, so an anonymous visitor can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs.
steps_to_exploit: Request the research page with no cookie and a url parameter
